questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question tests practical distributed tracing integration in a multi-data-center containerized environment. It validates OpenTelemetry fundamentals, OTLP export to Jaeger, and per-tenant configuration via Docker Config. The question also checks understanding of TLS termination and Traefik integration with trace context propagation across data centers.

## Key Concepts
- OpenTelemetry instrumentation and HTTP trace context propagation
- OTLP exporter configured to send spans to Jaeger collector
- Docker Config for dynamic per-tenant sampling rate settings
- Traefik trace header propagation for downstream services
- Multi-data-center service discovery and traffic routing with TLS

## Code Example
```javascript
// Node.js OpenTelemetry bootstrap
const { NodeSDK } = require('@opentelemetry/sdk-node');
const { getNodeAutoInstrumentations } = require('@opentelemetry/auto-instrumentations-node');
const { OTLPTraceExporter } = require('@opentelemetry/exporter-trace-otlp-grpc');

const sdk = new NodeSDK({
  serviceName: 'tenant-api',
  traceExporter: new OTLPTraceExporter({
    url: 'jaeger:4317'
  }),
  instrumentations: [getNodeAutoInstrumentations()]
});

sdk.start();
```

```yaml
# docker-compose.yml skeleton
services:
  traefik:
    image: traefik:v3.0
    ports:
      - "443:443"
    volumes:
      - ./certs:/certs
    command:
      - "--entrypoints.websecure.address=:443"
      - "--tls.cert=/certs/server.crt"
      - "--tls.key=/certs/server.key"
      - "--providers.docker"
      - "--providers.docker.exposedbydefault=false"

  api:
    build: .
    labels:
      - "traefik.enable=true"
      - "traefik.http.routers.api.tls=true"
      - "traefik.http.routers.api.rule=Host(`api.example.com`)"

  jaeger:
    image: jaegertracing/all-in-one:1.47
    ports:
      - "4317:4317"
      - "16686:16686"
```

```bash
# Bootstrap commands
docker config create tenant-tracing /path/to/tracing-config.json
docker stack deploy -c docker-compose.yml myapp
```

## Why This Is Asked

Assessing observability discipline in Docker Swarm: instrumenting code, sidecar collectors, and end-to-end tracing with Jaeger, while validating latency overhead.

## Key Concepts

- OpenTelemetry instrumentation and OTLP exporters
- Sidecar collector pattern in Swarm
- Jaeger backend and sampling configuration
- Docker secrets for TLS and Docker configs for routing
- Overlay network communication and minimal overhead

## Code Example

```yaml
# docker-compose skeleton (draft)
version: '3.8'
services:
  api:
    image: myapi:latest
    secrets:
      - tls_cert
      - tls_key
    configs:
      - source: endpoints
        target: /config/endpoints.json
    networks:
      - overlay
    deploy:
      replicas: 1
  otel-collector:
    image: otel/opentelemetry-collector-contrib:0.63.0
    volumes:
      - ./otel-config.yaml:/conf/otel-config.yaml
    command: ["--config", "/conf/otel-config.yaml"]
    networks:
      - overlay
    deploy:
      replicas: 1
networks:
  overlay:
    driver: overlay
secrets:
  tls_cert:
    file: ./certs/api.crt
  tls_key:
    file: ./certs/api.key
configs:
  endpoints:
    file: ./config/endpoints.json
```

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to extend a docker-dca deployment with tenant-aware observability and per-tenant gating using Docker Configs. Evaluates practical wiring of Traefik TLS, sidecar pattern, Prometheus remote_write, and config-driven tenancy.

## Key Concepts
- Tenant-tagged metrics and Prometheus remote_write
- Docker Config driven per-tenant namespaces
- Sidecar pattern and data-plane observability wiring
- Dockerdca bootstrap and minimal compose snippet

## Code Example
```yaml
# minimal docker-compose.yml sketch
version: '3.8'
services:
  api:
    image: my-api:latest
    networks:
      - app
    deploy:
      replicas: 2
    labels:
      - traefik.enable=true
      - traefik.http.routers.api.rule=Host(`api.example.com`)
    volumes:
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock
      - ./tls:/certs
    configs:
      - source: metrics-config
        target: /etc/metrics/metrics-config.yaml
  metrics-sink:
    image: tenant-metrics-sink:latest
    depends_on:
      - api
    configs:
      - source: metrics-config
        target: /etc/metrics/metrics-config.yaml
configs:
  metrics-config:
    external: true
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test tenant isolation for metrics in DC failover?

Why This Is Asked

- Multi-site Docker Swarm cluster management

Code Example

```yaml
# docker-compose.yml
version: '3.8'

services:
  nginx:
    image: nginx:alpine
    ports:
      - "443:443"
    volumes:
      - ./nginx.conf:/etc/nginx/nginx.conf
      - ./certs:/etc/nginx/certs
    depends_on:
      - api

  api:
    image: my-api:latest
    environment:
      - VAULT_ADDR=https://vault.example.com
      - SPIFFE_WORKLOAD_API=unix:///spiffe-agent/socket
    volumes:
      - /var/run/spiffe/agent:/spiffe-agent
    depends_on:
      - redis

  verifier:
    image: spiffe-verifier:latest
    volumes:
      - /var/run/spiffe/agent:/spiffe-agent

  opa:
    image: openpolicyagent/opa:latest
    command: run --server --addr=localhost:8181 /policy
    volumes:
      - ./policy:/policy

  rate-limiter:
    image: rate-limiter:latest
    environment:
      - REDIS_URL=redis://redis:6379
    depends_on:
      - redis

  redis:
    image: redis:alpine
    ports:
      - "6379:6379"

  vault:
    image: vault:latest
    environment:
      - VAULT_ADDR=https://vault.example.com
    ports:
      - "8200:8200"
```

Bootstrap Commands:

```bash
# Initialize Docker Swarm cluster
docker swarm init --advertise-addr <MANAGER_IP>

# Join worker nodes
docker swarm join --token <TOKEN> <MANAGER_IP>:2377

# Deploy stack
docker stack deploy -c docker-compose.yml secure-api

# Configure Vault for SPIFFE
vault secrets enable spiffe
vault write spiffe/config trust_domain "example.com"

# Initialize canary deployment
docker service update --replicas 1 --update-parallelism 1 --update-delay 10s secure-api_api
```
